items.summary: Nvidia lost about US$700 billion in market value over the past week after chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12 amid reports of a third alleged extramarital affair. Its share price fell more than 12%, its sixth straight weekly drop and longest losing streak since 2012, as Nvidia had lost about US$1. 8 trillion in market value since October. CFO Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while the board reportedly approached Arm Holdings' Rene Haas for a successor. Tech stocks fell again after opening higher on Nov 12, with AMD down more than 8% and Broadcom more than 4%. The Nasdaq closed 0. 9% lower and the S&P 500 fell 0. 4%, though Singapore tech stocks rebounded. Singtel CEO Yuen Kuan Moon sold 2 million shares for $8. 14 million, hours after raising operating profit growth guidance to mid- to high-single-digit for FY2027 on an 8.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Ousting Sends Tech Stocks Tumbling; Singtel CEO Sells Shares

items.summary: Indian equity markets ended the week higher, with modest gains across indices as banking and broader stocks outperformed. The coming week brings fresh domestic and global cues, including Nvidia's earnings amid Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, India's WPI data, US Federal Reserve minutes, and a possible US-India trade agreement. Three developments shaped sentiment last week: renewed FII buying, AI-trade concerns around Nvidia, and retail inflation rising above the RBI's 4-6% range.
items.title: Markets Next Week: Key Triggers for Dalal Street

items.summary: The Jensen Huang-Nvidia controversy, involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operation and his resignation on November 12, has spotlighted how US tech firms are bringing counterintelligence expertise in-house. OpenAI, Anthropic and ASML now recruit former intelligence officials; OpenAI hired retired NSA director Paul Nakasone and posts security roles paying $230,400-$500,000 plus equity. The trend extends to AI developers facing knowledge-distillation campaigns from China-based firms, prompting a 2026 senatorial letter and joint FBI-NSA-CISA advisories urging companies to detect foreign activity and share threat intelligence.
items.title: Silicon Valley Firms Hire Ex-Spies Against Foreign Espionage Threats

items.summary: The Nvidia spy scandal has drawn scrutiny to Malaysia as authorities investigate alleged intermediaries used to route high-performance chips toward China, bypassing US export controls. MITI intensified its investigation of Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd alongside the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, working with Singapore-based parent Megaspeed International Pte Ltd. Police reportedly opened an inquiry paper in April 2025 over claims that subsidiaries circumvented Nvidia AI chip restrictions.
items.title: Malaysia intensifies probe into Megaspeed and Speedmatrix over Nvidia spy scandal fallout

items.summary: Nvidia's longtime chief security officer David Reber stepped down in August, citing a young-onset Parkinson's diagnosis after four years as CSO and seven overall. CEO Jensen Huang followed two months later amid questions about extramarital relationships with employees, including an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company under federal investigation for funneling Nvidia chips to China. Nothing public links the security team's departures to these matters. Security specialists note that intelligence services often gather information through conversation rather than hacking, and that teams are frequently underfunded and narrowly defined around facilities and cyberattacks. Whether Nvidia's expansive remit caught these risks remains unclear as independent board and federal inquiries proceed.
items.title: Where was Nvidia’s security team?

items.summary: Italy fined Meta €805 million ($887 million) for letting Android users' gallery photos and videos be accessed on Facebook without specific consent. The feature “Get suggestions from gallery when browsing Facebook” was enabled by default under a single permission covering multiple functions, violating EU privacy law that treats smartphones as part of the private sphere. Meta had 60 days to disable it; its lack of cooperation factored into the penalty (~0.47% of global turnover). Italy has ~20 million Android users.
items.title: Meta Fined $887 Million in Italy Over Facebook's Access to Phone Photos, Videos

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, reportedly signed a $3.4 billion contract to purchase gas-fired power plants from OnePWR Solutions in Texas (s3). The article criticizes this as one of the largest single purchases of power-generation equipment by an AI lab and argues it signals the industry's turn away from renewables toward pollution-spewing gas generators (s6, s7). Anthropic's own Claude acknowledged that while gas is cleaner than coal, its climate impact depends on what it replaces and methane leak control (s8-s15). Separately, Sierra Club estimated upcoming AI data centers could release 2.1 billion metric tons of CO₂ by 2030 (s23), yet only one of 41 related ballot measures passed in recent elections (s25).
items.title: Anthropic's $3.4 Billion Gas Power Plant Order Draws Climate Criticism

items.summary: Overseas Congress chief Sam Pitroda responded to Rahul Gandhi's allegation that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is surveilling him. When asked, Pitroda denied the PM does such things but said someone is indeed attacking his telephone, laptops and bank accounts constantly. He declined to name who was behind it, leaving the matter for Gandhi to address.
items.title: Pitroda dismisses Rahul's claim that PM is tapping his phone

items.summary: The UK government will consider changing the age of consent after Mia Latter, now 37, publicly alleged she was orally raped by comedian Russell Brand when she was 16 and he was 30. She called for a staggered age of consent making relationships with 16- and 17-year-olds illegal. De facto deputy prime minister Louise Haigh said the 'heart-breaking story' deserved consideration, while Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson Jess Brown-Fuller praised her bravery and supported reviewing laws to address power imbalances. Bridget Phillipson commended her courage. Brand denies all allegations; he was convicted of attacks against four of six women and serves a 10-and-a-half-year term. Separately, serious sex offence allegations against David Walliams are being probed by the Metropolitan police.
items.title: UK Government Considers Changing Age of Consent After Russell Brand Allegations

items.summary: Dr Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga, a 30-year-old doctor in Butembo, North Kivu, contracted the Bundibugyo species of Ebola and became one of 3,031 survivors. His family feared he would die at the treatment centre, but his recovery proves survival is possible. Amid an outbreak that has killed 5,400 people and infected 11,000 since WHO declared it a public health emergency in July, Kamwanga combats misinformation through community outreach and writing his book, The Price of Saving Lives. He faces death threats, accusations of being paid, mistrust fueled by poverty and conflict trauma, and reports that Ebola funds are misappropriated while protective equipment is lacking.
items.title: Ebola Survivor's Fight for Awareness in DR Congo

items.summary: France's world heavyweight judo champion Teddy Riner, a Guadeloupe-born 37-year-old with five Olympic golds and an established business career, has entered next April's presidential election. His campaign so far rests on the slogan La France qu'on aime (The France we love), social media declarations, and a hospital visit in Seine-Saint-Denis. Polling shows roughly 28 million watched his broadcast, with about 22% saying they could vote for him. Commentators note that mocking Riner risks backfiring given the fractured centre-ground between Marine Le Pen's hard right and Jean-Luc Mélenchon's France Unbowed (LFI), who welcomed his candidacy as a distraction.
items.title: Judo champion Teddy Riner enters French presidential race amid political disarray

items.summary: Beauty advent calendars cost upwards of £100, sometimes much more, and are marketed with sophisticated tactics including scarcity warnings and influencer unboxing videos. Ipsos data shows around 15% of all advent calendars sold are beauty ones, especially among people aged 18-34. The Skims calendar scandal—where Kim Kardashian's brand refunded its $148 (£110) calendar after criticism over low-quality contents—is prompting savvier consumers to scrutinise what they buy. Some buyers report getting fragrances for less than retail and reselling unwanted items, while experts caution that using every product inside is unlikely.
items.title: Are Beauty Advent Calendars Value for Money?

items.summary: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Goyal addressed a community event organized by the Indian Community Association in Cairo, invoking the "Karmabhoomi" spirit to remind Indians abroad that India remains their homeland while they fulfill responsibilities toward Egypt. He highlighted the Bohra community's entrepreneurial role in strengthening people-to-people ties and economic relations, praised diaspora contributions through soldiers' sacrifices and job creation, and outlined his November 15-16 visit aimed at boosting bilateral trade, investment and industrial cooperation.
items.title: Goyal invokes 'Karmabhoomi' spirit in Cairo diaspora

items.summary: A bus collision near Tarn Taran, Punjab killed four people and injured eighteen. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the deaths. The accident occurred when a motorcyclist approached from the wrong side, prompting one bus driver to swerve; another bus coming from the opposite direction collided with it. Four died—three pilgrims and the motorcycle rider—while six critically injured were sent to Amritsar Medical College.
items.title: Bus Collision in Punjab Kills Four, Injures Eighteen

items.summary: Cacao is a six-year-old Pomeranian surrendered this spring when his family could no longer keep him. Angry and resistant to leashing seven months ago, he has since transformed into an affectionate dog who loves being brushed and running with boundless energy. Though spirited and confident by breed, Cacao wants participation in decisions affecting him; he is independent yet craves a devoted person whose life revolves around him.
items.title: Cacao, a spirited Pomeranian seeking his forever home at ARK

items.summary: Italy has formally proposed granting Germany observer status in the Global Combat Air Program (GCAP), a sixth-generation stealth fighter jet initiative it is developing with the United Kingdom and Japan, targeting service by the mid-2030s. This proposal contradicts an earlier report suggesting Italy opposed Berlin's involvement. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius anticipates a decision on joining GCAP by end of March, following Germany's cancellation of its Future Combat Air System project with France.
items.title: Italy Proposes Germany Observer Status in GCAP Fighter Program

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department reports a well-marked low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal is likely to become a depression by Sunday, intensify into a cyclonic storm on November 16 and possibly a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. Odisha faces substantial rainfall (12-20 cm) and squally winds; North Coastal Andhra Pradesh expects heavy-to-very-heavy rain with gusts to 70 kmph, while Gangetic West Bengal sees isolated heavy rain and wind gusts of 60 kmph by November 19. Disaster Minister Suresh Pujari urged vigilance amid lingering flood damage from Cyclone Arnab.
items.title: IMD weather update: Odisha braces for 3rd cyclone in three weeks; Andhra, Bengal and Andaman on high alert

items.summary: Released on 14th November 2026, datasette-llm version 0.1a11 adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, letting users configure Datasette to use any LLM that speaks the OpenAI web protocol. This enables running local models via LM Studio or Ollama through uvx.
items.title: datasette-llm 0.1a11

items.summary: On Saturday (Nov 15), SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from a 22-hour orbital voyage and became the first to be caught by the mechanical arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas. The two-stage rocket had orbited Earth 14 times before descending through clouds, reigniting engines to land vertically while still roaring. Mission commentator Dan Huot called it 'the missing link' for reusable spaceflight. Though SpaceX has spent more than US$15 billion developing the system—funded partly by NASA's US$3.2 billion of a contract worth over US$4 billion—the company has yet to recover both stages in one mission, and its heat shield remains only partially reusable.
items.title: SpaceX Starship Successfully Caught by Tower After Orbital Return

items.summary: Swiss luxury group Richemont reported net profit rising 39% to €2.5 billion for the six months to September, beating expectations as jewellery maisons drove growth while specialist watchmakers showed recovery.
items.title: Richemont Beats Luxury Downturn on Jewellery Strength and Watch Recovery

items.summary: Anthropic is pursuing an approximately $1.4 trillion valuation in its proposed IPO, priced at $70-78 per share under ticker ANT and potentially raising up to $64.4 billion. Its massive ~$901 billion compute commitments raise sustainability concerns: about $452 billion falls due before end of 2030. Revenue-per-compute-dollar ratios fell from $2.08 (Q2) to $1.72 (Q3), while operating break-even requires roughly $1.20-1.25 per dollar, according to Ashika Institutional Equities.
items.title: Anthropic's $1.4 Trillion IPO Faces a $901 Billion Compute Question

items.summary: Cryptocurrencies fell over the weekend as leveraged longs were liquidated, with Bitcoin dropping to a three-month low near US$63,000. Ether also slumped 8% to US$1,731. Analyst Rich Rosenblum of GSR called it a technical breakdown below the 200-day moving average around US$73,000, triggering liquidations and new shorts amid rate fears, ETF outflows and fallout from the Binance hack.
items.title: Bitcoin Hits Three-Month Low Amid Accelerating Crypto Liquidations

items.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said India ceased being a democracy in 2014, with institutions taken over by fascists. Speaking at Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad, he blamed the BJP-led NDA government for electoral manipulation and voter deletions via SIR. He claimed millions of dollars flooded politics after 2014, that seven million new voters were added to help BJP win Maharashtra's assembly polls three months after Congress won a majority, decimating his alliance.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Claims Democracy Destroyed in 2014

items.summary: David Jones' administration has prompted questions about its rival, Myer, whose profitability is battered and share price near lows. Although Myer reported double-digit sales growth to $4. 1bn last financial year (s4), this was driven by acquisitions from Premier Investments rather than demand, while heavy discounting reduced profits and brand value fell over $200m in a year (s7). Department stores face sustained relevance erosion as online platforms win shoppers (s8). Myer's key advantage is time: it finished with a $100m net cash buffer (s14) and cut store numbers to 56 from 60 pre-pandemic (s15), unlike the collapsed Jones. With roughly two in five stores sharing centres with David Jones outlets, investors hope DJ closures boost Myer's market share (s25). Analysts Richard Hemming of Under The Radar Report and Brian Walker of The Retail Doctor Group see both upside from early restructuring and ongoing vulnerability amid cost-of-living pressures squeezing discretionary spending.
items.title: Is Myer Next After David Jones?

items.summary: A nearly five-hour shutdown of the US aviation system, disrupting more than 20,000 flights since Friday, may have been caused by a single router installed by government contractor L3Harris. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the FAA's ageing telecom systems did not meet modern demands and that officials had yet to determine whether the fault stemmed from user error or a defective device. The incident began when new routers flooded other units with over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, causing instability at 17 of the agency's 22 en route centres. Officials suspect problems with routers in Arkansas and Texas, where L3Harris was switching lines from copper to fibre-optic cabling. The FAA has spent $1 billion annually maintaining its outdated system while pursuing upgrades funded partly by a $12.5 billion congressional allocation.
items.title: L3Harris Router May Have Triggered US Aviation System Shutdown

items.summary: This edition traces how the Kannada track 'Neeve Nanna Thayi Thande' by Vijaya Anand (later known as A. R. Rahman) reached Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories, after American couple Amy Sillman and Kurt Hoffman found a bootleg cassette of his 1987 film Dance Raja Dance and shared it with Luaka Bop's David Byrne. It then examines why the Netherlands is closing prisons despite falling crime worldwide—its prison population dropped from 20,463 in 2006 to 12,570 in 2025, roughly 70 per lakh versus 542 in the US—as prosecutors handle cases without judges or incarceration and favor rehabilitation. The Netherlands rents surplus cells abroad and converts closed prisons into cinemas and hotels, though this risks job losses (around 2,000) and future overcrowding.
items.title: A Kannada song's unlikely path into GTA; why Dutch prisons are closing

items.summary: Filipino singer Carmelle won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest on Saturday (Nov 14) with her dance-pop anthem Sobra-Sobra, beating 10 other acts at a grand final in Bangkok. At 19, she said the song celebrated female empowerment as a tribute to Filipino women.
items.title: Carmelle Wins Inaugural Eurovision Asia Song Contest in Bangkok

items.summary: Khan Shamim Akhtar, a Mumbai artist born in Kurla in 1994 who holds a Master's at the JJ School of Art, has sustained work about Gaza. He won several awards including the South Asia Speaks Prize 2026 and was selected as a curator for the Students' Biennale at the Kochi-Muziris Biennale. His korai-mat paintings—Stone of Survival, Bereaved, Humanity in a Bag—and his RIP Book installation list over 3,500 dead names from Gaza's Ministry of Health.
items.title: Artist Khan Shamim Akhtar and His Gaza Work from Mumbra

items.summary: Caregivers report that navigating the NDIS for more support is exhausting and damaging to their mental health amid funding cuts rolled out from October 1. Amanda Solarino, full-time carer in Romsey, describes her autistic son's escalating aggression breaking furniture costing thousands, while Breanna Medcalfe on the Sunshine Coast relies on her parents as informal supports after declining NDIS requests.
items.title: Carers of People with Disability Left Exhausted Navigating NDIS

items.summary: Aryna Sabalenka apologized Saturday for an angry outburst during her Friday round-robin loss to Ukraine's Elina Svitolina at the Indian Wells WTA Finals. Footage suggested she swore, with some social media users believing it targeted Svitolina or Ukrainians. Sabalenka clarified her comment was not aimed at Elina, blaming aggressive spectators and saying she should have reacted differently.
items.title: Sabalenka Apologizes for Outburst After WTA Finals Loss to Svitolina

items.summary: The Al-Qassam Brigades confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, a senior commander who helped plan the October 7 attack and led its Rafah brigade, was killed Saturday in an Israeli drone strike on Khan Younis. Medics said he died with several others wounded. The killing occurred despite an October 2025 ceasefire; Gaza health authorities report at least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed since.
items.title: Hamas Confirms Killing of Senior Commander Samir Abu Younis in Israeli Strike

items.summary: The US National Transportation Safety Board has launched a fact-finding investigation into the Friday collision between tanker Atlantic Asphalt and cruise ship American Heritage in New Orleans, where all 197 passengers and crew survived. NTSB member John DeLeeuw said it is too soon to determine cause; a preliminary report follows within 30 days and final findings in 18-24 months. Port officials hold the tanker after $1.47 million terminal damage.
items.title: NTSB Opens Investigation Into New Orleans Tanker-Cruise Ship Collision After All Survive

items.summary: Congress MLA Harish Dhami, chairperson of the 10-day Jauljibi Mela in Pithoragarh district, allegedly vandalised its inauguration stage after claiming he was denied a chance to speak before Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. Congress workers staged a protest objecting to the non-invitation of MLA Mayukh Singh Mahar. BJP leaders condemned the incident and abusive language, attributing it to frustration as Congress loses ground in Dharchula.
items.title: Congress MLA vandalises stage at Uttarakhand event: ‘Denied chance to speak before CM Dhami’

items.summary: Oncologist Siddhartha Mukherjee, co-founder of Manas AI, argued that artificial intelligence has compressed the time to design new medicines from years to months. He illustrated this with daraxonrasib: a human researcher spent about ten years finding its target keyhole, while his algorithm did so in two hours; work once taking seven to eight years now takes three to four months. Yet clinical testing remains unchanged and risky—AI cannot resolve the mid-stage trial coin flip or avoid 'bias in, bias out' from simulated data. Mukherjee urged safeguards like conditional approval with withdrawal after two or three years. He called India's reform of drug regulation a historic opportunity, citing Immuneel and its AI-made synthetic binder for blood cancers. A medicine costing $500,000 in the United States is now sold for $35,000 in India.
items.title: Siddhartha Mukherjee at HT Leadership Summit on AI and drug design

items.summary: CGTN commentators Zhang Jianping and Gao Yuan argue that Asia-Pacific cooperation depends on openness, which Xi Jinping has framed through metaphors of geese flying together, sweet-potato vines sharing roots, and fellow passengers in one boat. The region hosts nearly 40% of the world's population, accounts for about 50% of global trade and over 60% of economic output, and is projected to drive 68% of growth in 2026. China has cut its overall tariff level from 9.8% in 2014 to 7.3% by 2024.
items.title: How APEC Can Keep Its Lifeline Open

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi used his valedictory address at the two-day Bharat Summit in Hyderabad to argue that India is no longer a democracy, framing it within a broader global decline of democratic institutions. Speaking before delegates from around 70 countries, he emphasized peaceful political struggle and asserted confidence that Congress and its allies would defeat the BJP by 2029. Salman Khurshid clarified during press briefings that the summit aimed to exchange ideas rather than interfere in any country's internal affairs, distancing India's situation from developments in Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The BJP is likely to accuse Gandhi of embarrassing the government and seeking regime change through unconstitutional means. Domestically, Rahul projected Telangana as a progressive gathering place akin to Davos while reasserting Congress's lost moral leadership on the world stage.
items.title: What Bharat Summit Means for Congress at Home and abroad

items.summary: University students across China spent a year building their own robots before converging in Shenzhen for an annual head-to-head competition, described as unlike any other. The event draws university teams to the city, where its appetite for innovation meets the next generation of engineering talent. Author Zak Dychtwald found himself on the edge of his seat watching the contest unfold. The article frames this as a showcase of student-driven robotics and emerging engineering capability in China's competitive landscape.
items.title: China's University Robot Showdown in Shenzhen

items.summary: This article examines the allegation that Alice Huang, managing director of Singapore-based Megaspeed International with Nvidia business dealings, was a Chinese spy deployed to defame Jensen Huang. The claim gained traction because it cast her as a 'woman spy,' evoking historical figures like Mata Hari and Noor Inayat Khan. The piece draws parallels to India's 1994 ISRO spy scandal involving aerospace engineer Nambi Narayanan in Thiruvananthapuram, which was later disproved by 1996 as a fabricated case rooted in local misconduct rather than genuine espionage.
items.title: The Alice Huang Spy Allegation and Its Echoes in Past Espionage Narratives

items.summary: With just over two months until its general election, Nigeria faces mounting concerns as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) released a preliminary voters' register reportedly riddled with AI-generated images. Signs include exaggerated facial features and inconsistencies such as duplicated names and identities of deceased individuals, raising fears about preparedness ahead of 2027. INEC chairman Joash Amupitan announced an investigation and the creation of a dedicated unit to detect deepfakes. Experts warn that beyond influencing voter behavior through inflated crowds, AI's deeper danger may be eroding public trust in authentic information itself. Nigeria has previously battled fabricated content during its 2023 election.
items.title: Nigeria's Upcoming Election Marred by Rising AI Disinformation

items.summary: Following US strikes on Iran and President Trump's November 9 claim that the conflict was 'effectively over,' DW Fact Check investigated a network of pro-Iran content farms. NewsGuard found 165 false claims watched hundreds of millions of times, while ISD identified coordinated X networks with no state links. The account 'Iran Military Media' alone has 290,000 X followers and generated 150 million views since late 2025 across over 1,600 posts. Ten similar accounts reached 353 million combined views. Analysts attribute this to Ayatollah Khamenei's 'soft war' strategy.
items.title: Iranian Content Farms Reach Millions of Views Amid Regional Conflict

items.summary: This article demystifies five common skincare myths about pigmentation, acne and uneven skin tone that stem from the visibility factor driving quick fixes. Dr Shallu Kapiil of Skinique explains ads use fear to promote instant results, while dermatologist Dr Soma Sarkar warns wrong products delay proper treatment. Myth 1: hot water opens pores; reality is tepid cleansing avoids stripping lipids. Myth 2: oily skin needs no moisturiser; oiliness differs from hydration. Myth 3: natural means safe; raw aloe vera and essential oils can irritate, though formulated synthetics offer consistency. Myth 4: sunscreen for sunny days only; UVA passes clouds and glass. Myth 5: any suggested product works; bleaching agents, lemon slices, saliva or toothpaste damage skin. Experts urge evidence-based choices guided by professionals.
items.title: Five Skincare Myths That Could Harm Your Skin

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron warned Saturday that limiting aid to Ukraine would force Kyiv into an "unjust peace" and risk another war, calling it a recipe for defeat. His remarks accompany US-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, which ended without breakthrough but agreed European nations—France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland—would join future negotiations. Zelensky said Washington suggested Kyiv cede Donbas to gain NATO membership.
items.title: Macron Warns Limiting Ukraine Aid Risks 'Another War'

items.summary: The article argues that people increasingly consult friends, parents and social media before even small choices like what to wear or whether to take up new courses. While advice is helpful, relying on too many opinions creates confusion and erodes decision-making skills, leaving exciting plans stressful rather than empowering. Counsellor Bhavika Agarwal warns that 'too many cooks spoil the broth,' urging readers to make their own decisions while listening only to those with relevant experience. Young traveler Mihir Vaidya shares how he pursued a one-year exchange program in Brasil despite varied reactions, crediting his parents' support for his success.
items.title: Is Your Life Becoming A Group Project? Here's Why You Should Trust Your Own Decisions

items.summary: Russia has softened its stance on European involvement in upcoming peace talks with Ukraine, signaling for the first time it would not oppose an EU delegation. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated Moscow had no intention to dictate who represents Europe at negotiations, marking a shift from earlier rhetoric accusing Brussels of prolonging the war. This follows trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks and Kushner's announcement expanding participation; EU leaders agreed Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland would represent it.
items.title: Moscow Says It Will Not Dictate EU Delegation's Participation in Ukraine Talks

items.summary: European Union leaders champion maximum electrification to cut dependence on imported energy, yet electricity prices recently surged past 600 euros per MWh amid a wind drought while the bloc still relies on over 70% hydrocarbons. The European Commission's plan aims to raise electricity's share of final energy consumption from 23% today to 46% by 2040, emphasizing domestic renewable sources. However, seasonal lulls in wind and solar output force reliance on imports or gas—now at record-low EU stockpiles—with grid upgrades estimated to cost over half a trillion euros by 2030. Analysts warn the transition may not deliver cheap, reliable energy as promised.
items.title: EU's Electrification Ambition Collides With Energy Reality

items.summary: The Trump administration says Friday's four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop, which delayed or canceled thousands of flights, stemmed from routine maintenance. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the issues began when a contractor switched telecommunications lines from copper wire to fiber optic cable at a remote FAA facility; officials are investigating whether it was incompetence or faulty equipment. The longest such stop in 25 years left passengers stranded across the US on Saturday, with more than 4,000 flights canceled by 11am ET and over 8,000 recorded Friday alone. Officials see no evidence of a nefarious or AI-related cause. Affected travel included college football, basketball, NBA and NHL games, plus disruptions in Boston, Washington DC, New York and Miami. Airlines warned of continued delays while the FAA urged Congress to fully fund a new air traffic control system.
items.title: US FAA Ground Stop Attributed to Routine Maintenance Amid Travel Chaos

items.summary: Dozens of Portuguese cities saw protests Saturday against the housing shortage, with demonstrators demanding rent caps and more public housing. The unrest coincides with a new government bill that would speed up evictions and remove rent controls. Portugal records the third largest rise in housing costs in Europe at 60.8% between 2015 and 2025, ahead of the Netherlands' 34.3%. Foreign investment and tourism have driven prices sharply upward while incomes stagnate.
items.title: Portugal's Housing Crisis Sparks Nationwide Protests Amid New Eviction Bill

items.summary: Dongfeng Nissan opened pre-orders for the new NX7 plug-in hybrid, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery at an MSRP around $20,000. Positioned as a practical 'long-range hybrid,' it is framed against earlier models like the first-generation Nissan LEAF and the upcoming 2027 Rogue Hybrid. The NX7 pairs a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated engine producing 98 hp with a 228 hp electric motor, drawing on Dongfeng's four-mode hybrid architecture (series, parallel, direct drive, generation). Buyers receive Model Y-sized dimensions, a 17.3-inch touchscreen, and optional features including a 55-inch augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8295P running Nissan OS 3.0 with an iFlytek-developed voice assistant.
items.title: $20K Dongfeng Nissan NX7 PHEV Offers Near-200-Mile Electric Range

items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday, halting all departures and landings across US airports for just over four hours. Officials Markwayne Mullin and Sean Duffy suggested the outage stemmed from older technology being overwhelmed by data after new systems were introduced. The shutdown was the longest since 9/11 and only the second of its kind.
items.title: Rare Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Halts US Air Traffic

items.summary: Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen said COP31 in Antalya must demonstrate that multilateralism still delivers results amid a global 'polycrisis' of wars, energy insecurity and cost-of-living pressures. He urged governments to keep backing renewable energy investment while remaining committed to limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius under the Paris Agreement. Negotiations are progressing on just transition, mitigation and climate finance work programmes. Bowen highlighted small island developing states receiving only 0.2% of global climate finance for adaptation and pointed to a new working group with Australia, the UK and partners to improve access.
items.title: Australian Minister Bowen on COP31 Amid Global Polycrisis

items.summary: On November 14th, 2026, Simon will release a new version of Datasette's longest untouched plugin for rendering charts with Vega-Lite against table or custom-query data. The last release was in July 2018; this update adds compatibility with the latest Datasette alphas and cosmetic tweaks to improve support for Datasette Lite, which recently gained JavaScript-plugin capability.
items.title: datasette-vega 0.7

items.summary: A 61-year-old Canadian woman traveled to India on a tourist visa after meeting Nitin, a Panipat-based teacher, through a dating app. Their relationship soured when he learned her age and refused the marriage. After contacting the Canadian Embassy, police took both into custody at Neemrana's BB Builders Society around 4 am on November 14; Nitin was charged with disturbing public peace but released on bail, while she remains in Kotputli detention as authorities arrange her return to Canada.
items.title: Canadian woman, 61, reaches Rajasthan for marriage; man backs out, police step in

items.summary: Phnom Penh is hosting the 20th Francophonie Summit this Sunday and Monday, with French President Emmanuel Macron attending as part of a 3-day state visit to Cambodia. Despite France and Cambodia's deep-rooted and complex history, the two countries share one common passion: pétanque.
items.title: France and Cambodia Share Their Love for Pétanque in Phnom Penh

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh will offer its first-ever online self-enumeration option, running from November 16 to 30, before enumerators visit every household. Households can submit details via census.gov.in and receive a unique SE ID retrievable by the enumerator through an app. The full exercise, including caste enumeration, spans December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027, with a reference date of midnight on January 4-5, 2027.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Launches Online Self-Enumeration for Census 2027

items.summary: An IEA report frames accelerating renewable energy deployment in Southeast Asia as a response to intensifying energy security challenges, with the Iran war since February sharply reducing fuel trade and prompting governments to diversify away from imported oil and LNG. Per capita demand has risen nearly 30% over the past decade while crude output fell 40% below its 1990s peak. The IEA forecasts electricity demand rising about 5.4% annually through 2030, requiring major grid investment. Across Asia-Pacific excluding China, renewable capacity is expected to expand by more than 840 GW between 2026 and 2031, reaching nearly 1,700 GW total—more than doubling prior additions—with India accounting for roughly half the growth. Solar photovoltaics are projected to lead at around 80% of new capacity.
items.title: Iran War Accelerates Southeast Asia's Renewable Energy Push

items.summary: Former bureaucrats wrote Chief Minister Joseph Vijay urging the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government to restore a three-member High-Level Committee disbanded on November 6, which had reviewed Union-state relations since April 2025. The panel, headed by former Supreme Court judge Kurian Joseph, recommended restoring State List subjects and warned that transferring its February report's second part to the state law commission risks losing institutional knowledge.
items.title: Ex-Bureaucrats Urge Tamil Nadu to Restore Centre-State Relations Committee

items.summary: The Daily Mail announced a boycott of Formula 1 coverage after the FIA revoked Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season. The ban followed his Nov. 4 column criticizing Charles Leclerc, whom he called a “sneaky little bastard” over an opening-lap clash with Lewis Hamilton at Mexico City. Daily Mail head Chris Dean condemned it as an attack on press freedom.
items.title: Daily Mail Boycotts Formula 1 After FIA Bans Journalist Over Leclerc Criticism

items.summary: A Washington joke holds that presidential campaigns begin immediately after midterms, and it contains a grain of truth: even before all votes are counted, Democrats and Republicans already raise money, plan strategies, and assess potential candidates. With two years until 2028, the article notes there is no time to waste, listing politicians most often mentioned as possible presidential contenders—though none has confirmed they intend to run.
items.title: Eleven Names to Watch in the Race for the White House in 2028

items.summary: Ten days after what is being called one of the most consequential midterm victories in modern U.S. history, Democrats face converting an electoral backlash against Donald Trump into a durable governing project. Their top priority is controlling soaring prices on gasoline, housing, food and healthcare—though Trump will remain president for two more years with veto power. The party shows little interest in impeachment or culture-war battles over transgender rights. With 255 House seats, Democrats hold a comfortable majority cushion above the 218 needed. Success came across nearly every region except Florida and was delivered by centrists rather than left-wing figures like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. A wide field of potential 2028 presidential candidates is still emerging.
items.title: Democrats Look Ahead to 2028 After Midterm Gains

items.summary: Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces gunmen killed at least 44 civilians across northeastern DRC this week, following a separate attack that took 66 lives in North Kivu. The raids struck villages near Mambasa territory where Ebola was first detected six months ago. With three health workers among the dead and medical facilities burned, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned chronic instability hampers the response to an epidemic that has already caused more than 5,400 deaths.
items.title: IS-Linked ADF Attack Leaves at Least 44 Dead in DR Congo's Ituri

items.summary: The article argues that record midterm turnout reshaped Congress ahead of its January 2027 term, with significant implications for climate and clean energy policy. Although not everyone named climate change as a top issue, it influenced many voters concerned about electricity costs, data center proliferation, corruption, and inequality. The author asserts the Trump administration's fossil fuel agenda has driven up energy prices and worsened climate risks, including an imminent global 1. 5°C overshoot. She outlines what the new Congress can do: fund science and resilience agencies like NOAA, FEMA, and EPA; reverse attacks on clean energy laws such as the Bipartisan Infrastructure Act and Inflation Reduction Act; hold officials accountable through oversight; halt fossil fuel giveaways; support disaster recovery via FEMA; and sue over actions violating law or science.
items.title: What the US Midterm Elections Mean for Climate Progress

items.summary: The resignation of Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang is one of the most astonishing corporate scandals in memory, featuring allegations of international espionage and extramarital affairs. After 33 years as CEO, Huang resigned on Thursday amid reports of two additional affairs with Nvidia employees, causing the company’s stock to plummet—the Nasdaq fell 4% immediately after his departure. Investigations reveal a suspected relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, who ran Singapore-based Megaspeed datacenter firm, which may have facilitated billions in advanced chip transfers to China. The Chinese government denied involvement, calling reports “nothing but a smear.” Security experts say the affair reflects human vulnerability: intelligence analysts note that honeypot-style traps exploit consistent weaknesses in people seeking relationships or leverage. Experts warn no amount of training can replace personal judgment.
items.title: ‘Jensen Huang lost his mind’: how AI’s smartest man fell for the world’s oldest trick

items.summary: CGTN invites Bert Hofman, former World Bank country director for China, Mongolia and Korea, to revisit Shenzhen this autumn in a feature titled "Shenzhen: The Making of a Miracle." Over four decades the city has transformed from a small fishing village into a manufacturing powerhouse and global technology hub. The program explores how government policy and entrepreneurship shaped its rise, how it attracted first foreign investment, and how that foundation enabled homegrown technology giants.
items.title: Bert Hofman revisits Shenzhen: Exploring the forces behind its rise

items.summary: Yi Yingnan, a research fellow at Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies, argues that Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang's admitted extramarital affair must not be politicized into another "balloon incident." After acknowledging the scandal on November 8, 2026, Nvidia shares fell sharply. The controversy escalated from private conduct to an espionage narrative when US congressional committees summoned Huang amid claims of Chinese intelligence ties—a frame that requires no evidence and risks capital punishment. China's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations as baseless. Yingnan contends the affair is fundamentally a corporate governance crisis with only secondary export-control implications, warning against converting ethnicity or business lobbying into national-security accusations.
items.title: The Jensen Huang affair must not become another "balloon incident"

items.summary: On Saturday, SpaceX's Starship made history by becoming the first orbital rocket to return from space and land upright in its launch tower's mechanical arms at Starbase, Texas. The 15th flight reached orbit, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, then returned after more than 20 hours. Defense Secretary Hegseth praised Musk as a 'great American,' while Google CEO Sundar Pichai called the catch still feeling like science fiction.
items.title: SpaceX Starship Completes Historic Orbital Catch; Hegseth and Pichai React

items.summary: The US Department of Labor warned companies against treating temporary work visas as a core business strategy, signaling suspensions and deeper fraud investigations. Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito stressed that programs like the H-1B visa are stopgaps for when no qualified American is available, not permanent hiring methods. This follows October's suspension of Microsoft, Adobe, and six outsourcing firms—including Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant, and Capgemini—from the PERM green card program amid allegations they replaced American workers with lower-paid foreign employees. The administration has imposed a $100,000 payment requirement on certain new H-1B petitions and extended restrictions through September 2027, though no full shutdown of the visa system is imminent.
items.title: US Visa Crackdown Targets Indian IT Firms on H-1B and Green Card Abuse Allegations

items.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have acquired Strancally Castle, a historic Gothic Revival estate in County Waterford, Ireland. The transaction was registered at €51.17 million (about $57 million or ₹538 crore) for the principal residence and up to one acre of land. The property sits on roughly 440 acres beside the River Blackwater and includes a three-storey mansion with woodland, open land and a private jetty.
items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Buys Historic Castle in Ireland

items.summary: A Washington Post report says Marco Rubio sent President Trump a memo, using stronger language than the underlying CIA findings to flag former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an intelligence-linked Chinese businesswoman and its security implications. The disclosure intensified debates over advanced chip sales to China, where hawks opposed Huang's push for continued access. Reports of affairs followed his November 12 resignation as chief executive.
items.title: Rubio's Memo Scrutinizes Jensen Huang's China Ties Amid Nvidia Exit

items.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai praised SpaceX for catching its Starship spacecraft upright at launch site, calling it science fiction. The 15th flight reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites before a controlled return over ~22.5 hours. Super Heavy booster used 33 Raptor engines but aborted early due to low fuel; the catch marks progress toward full rocket reuse.
items.title: 'Feels like Sci-Fi': Google's Pichai hails Starship

items.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to hold a historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on November 19 (local time), hosted by Xi at this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. The gathering would mark an unprecedented assembly of leaders from the world's three biggest nuclear powers, confirmed first by the White House then the Kremlin. Discussions may touch Iran war, a new nuclear arms treaty after New START expired in February, and US-China trade rivalry over AI microchips. However, officials expect no agreements; Nvidia's spy scandal and Russia's nearly five-year-old Ukraine war are likely to be off-limits.
items.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting next week: Iran war on agenda, but Nvidia and Ukraine likely off the table

items.summary: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman dismisses space data centers as impractical for another decade or two, questioning the economics of orbital computing infrastructure. While Google's Project Suncatcher and SpaceX pursue plans to run AI hardware in orbit—SpaceX applied to launch up to one million satellites—Garman cites expensive launches, equipment weight, cooling challenges, radiation exposure, and servicing difficulties. He favors desert locations for terrestrial data centers instead.
items.title: AWS CEO Skeptical of Space Data Centers

items.summary: An analysis by the anti-corruption group DeKleptocracy, reported by The Guardian, found that President Donald Trump purchased between $1 million and $5 million in Nvidia shares. The transaction occurred in May 2025, one day before his administration revoked a Biden-era restriction on advanced AI chip exports to China under the AI Diffusion Framework. Nvidia's share price rose after the policy reversal cleared sales in a market that previously accounted for roughly a quarter of its revenue.
items.title: Trump's Nvidia Stock Purchase Ahead of China Chip Policy Shift

items.summary: Indian equities rebounded sharply as global funds rotated out of crowded AI trades toward markets with strong earnings, turning the country's low AI exposure into an advantage. The MSCI India gauge rose 11% from a six-month low, adding over $400 billion and nearly erasing 2026 losses. Overseas investors bought a net $8.5 billion in November—the biggest inflow in six years—while active funds remain about $74 billion underweight. Earnings growth is accelerating toward ~18% year-on-year, valuations look attractive at roughly 20 times forward profits, and lower oil prices help an energy-importing market.
items.title: AI Retreat Fuels India Stock Comeback in Great Rotation Trade

items.summary: Canada's Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu expressed confidence that India will be the next free trade agreement concluded, with CEPA negotiations targeting a December deadline set by Prime Ministers Modi and Carney. Following ASEAN talks in Manila alongside PM Mark Carney, Sidhu stressed Canada consulted businesses before pursuing the deal. The objective is to double bilateral trade to CA$70 billion by 2030.
items.title: India-Canada Free Trade Deal May Be Concluded Next Month

items.summary: As China hosts APEC for the third time, focus turns to three key priorities: openness, innovation and cooperation. This CGTN special episode, "The Power of Ideas: Together for a Brighter Asia-Pacific," gathers voices across the region to examine APEC's role in today's shifting global landscape and explore how cooperation can build a more resilient, connected and prosperous Asia-Pacific.
items.title: APEC's Third China Hostship and Its Openness, Innovation, Cooperation Priorities

items.summary: APEC 2026 prioritizes innovation, with artificial intelligence at its center as it reshapes the global economy rapidly. The central question is whether AI will widen development gaps or serve as a new engine for regional growth. Li Haitao, dean of Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business, argues that AI is profoundly rewiring globalization and opening new possibilities for multilateral cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region.
items.title: AI and the Future of Asia-Pacific Cooperation

items.summary: The Election Commission (EC) told the Supreme Court it remains committed to ensuring eligible voters are included in electoral rolls while addressing inconsistencies during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). In an affidavit, reported by PTI, the EC clarified that voters missing from draft rolls could apply afresh via Form 6 without prosecution. It directed chief electoral officers to publicise this widely and noted outreach to ASDD voters. The Commission cited challenges from large voter numbers and digitalisation while affirming its constitutional duty.
items.title: Election Commission Reassures Supreme Court on Voter Roll Consistency During SIR Exercise

items.summary: During the four-day Sun-worship festival of Chhath Puja, devotees descend on the polluted Yamuna in Delhi, believing faith shields them from its contamination. The river has become a recurring political battleground: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari praised cleanup work while AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar floated his effigy and challenged him to bathe at a stretch he called more polluted; ministers accuse each other over staged dead-fish videos near Sonia Vihar, with AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj demanding an inquiry. Chhath's political salience stems from Delhi's shifting demography—continued migration has raised the Purvanchali community to about 30 percent of the population—and the government is setting up 1,482 ghats across 996 locations. Environmentalist Saumya Dutta notes that low post-monsoon flow concentrates pollutants in this short stretch, which contributes roughly 70-80% of the river's pollution load; he blames ongoing sewage and industrial effluent inflow for cleaning failures.
items.title: How Chhath Puja Turns Delhi's Yamuna Into a Political and Pollution Flashpoint

items.summary: Australia's Albanese welcomed the historic Trump-Xi-Putin summit in Shenzhen, likened to Yalta 1945, while European leaders like Merz and Macron warned against an unjust peace. Zelensky cautioned against influence redistribution over Ukraine. Meanwhile, Australia strengthened ties with the Philippines through a defence agreement signed at Port of Manila.
items.title: Albanese Backs Trump-Xi-Putin Summit Amid European Caution and Pacific Defence Push

items.summary: British sportswear firm Gymshark, valued at £1.25bn after US investor General Atlantic joined in 2020, is fighting founder John Watson's small gym The Conditioning Club over a trademark clash. Founded by Ben Francis and now worth £800m, Gymshark applied to register the name for retail classes while opposing Watson's original registration as generic.
items.title: Gymshark Trademark Battle Threatens Small Fitness Business

items.summary: At UFC 334 in New York, Kayla Harrison retained her bantamweight title with a fourth-round rear-naked choke submission of Amanda Nunes. The 36-year-old judo champion overcame the Brazilian's early striking and takedown defense before applying grappling dominance to force the submission at age 38.
items.title: Kayla Harrison Retains UFC Bantamweight Title Over Amanda Nunes at UFC 334

items.summary: President Donald Trump is set to meet Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping Thursday on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China. The trilateral talks, described as unprecedented, are expected to yield few concrete results but carry heavy symbolism that analysts and former officials warn could set a worrying precedent for U.S. allies.
items.title: Trump-Putin-Xi Meeting Likely Short on Substance

items.summary: On Sunday (Nov 15), Bahrain issued two threat alerts—its first since September—as Iran claimed it had attacked a US air-defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base with six drones. The Revolutionary Guards cited retaliation for hostile US actions, though neither Washington nor Manama confirmed the strike; the US said it intercepted two Iranian drones without damage. Bahrain urged calm amid uncertainty over a stalled US-Iran deal.
items.title: Bahrain Issues First Threat Alerts Since September as Iran Claims US Base Attack

items.summary: In an interview with PTI, Escorts Kubota Ltd CFO Bharat Madan said the company plans to begin commercial construction of a greenfield tractor facility near Jewar airport in Uttar Pradesh early next fiscal year. The initial phase-one capacity is 60,000 units, scalable up to one lakh (100,000) tractors, with completion expected in about two and a half years.
items.title: Escorts Kubota Plans New Uttar Pradesh Tractor Plant with 60,000-Unit Capacity

items.summary: Mahesh Iyer, MD-CEO of Thomas Cook (India) Ltd, says the demerger of its resorts business into Sterling Holiday Resorts is expected to become effective by mid-FY28 or October 2027, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. The company remains open to acquisitions and partnerships, especially technology-led platforms across leisure travel, corporate travel and forex. India Travel businesses recovered sharply in Q2 FY27, ending just 6% below the prior year with EBIT margins of 3.8%, while forward bookings for Q3 FY27 are expected at 30%. The plans follow a recovery in demand after geopolitical disruptions.
items.title: Thomas Cook India Aims for October 2027 Resorts Demerger and Eyes Acquisitions

items.summary: As foreign nationals increasingly join Japan's workforce, diversity and inclusion have gained importance, prompting Japanese organizations to adopt training programs, policies and commitments toward inclusive workplaces amid talent-attraction challenges. However, a Nikkei survey earlier this year surfaced 'DEI fatigue,' citing frustration over excessive numerical targets for women's advancement, ineffective training and perceived unfairness—suggesting the backlash reflects how DEI is practiced rather than diversity itself.
items.title: Japan's DEI Backlash Amid Rising Foreign Workforce

items.summary: A man allegedly linked to incidents in Tasmania's north-west, including a service station robbery in Railton and the theft of a silver Alfa Romeo from Kimberley, is in police custody after a multi-hour search. Police were notified shortly after 9am Sunday when he was reported acting erratically on Macfie Street in Devonport before knocking on doors demanding vehicle keys. He fled to Penguin about 30 kilometres west of Devonport and surrendered near Preservation Bay just before 5pm.
items.title: Police helicopter joins search for Railton servo robbery suspect

items.summary: A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government from closing East Potomac Golf Links in Washington DC, which President Donald Trump planned to shut on 15 November for a 15-month renovation. Judge Ana Reyes ruled the administration's justifications were pretextual and that it violated at least two federal laws by meeting an arbitrary deadline.
items.title: Judge Blocks Trump's Closure of DC Golf Course for Renovation

items.summary: This Euronews news bulletin from November 15th, 2026 offers a fast-paced round-up of the most important stories across Europe and beyond. In just a few minutes, its newsroom delivers latest and breaking developments spanning world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, providing context to help viewers make sense of a rapidly evolving day with an independent European perspective.
items.title: Latest news bulletin | November 15th, 2026 – Morning

items.summary: On his first Latin America tour (elected May 2025), Pope Leo XIV visited Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, a village of about 6,000 people in the Cajamarca region of northern Peru's Andes. He spoke of community suffering from forced migration and declining birth rates emptying villages, noting over 40% of the region lives in poverty - its highest figure nationally. The town drew roughly 20,000; he returned by helicopter on Saturday before heading to Cusco and the Amazon, concluding his trip Monday back in Rome.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV visits remote Andean town amid regional poverty and migration

items.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi alleged on Saturday that democracy in India was destroyed when the Bharatiya Janata Party came to power in 2014. Speaking at the Congress-led Telangana government's Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, he accused the ruling party of weakening democratic institutions through massive money infusion into politics and declaring millions of voters illegal non-voters. Gandhi also criticized the blurred line between political power and business interests involving Narendra Modi and Gautam Adani.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Alleges Democracy Destroyed in India Since 2014 BJP Victory

items.summary: The Federal Court has declared the farm-tourism permit for Lorella Springs Wilderness Park, a 400,000-hectare cattle station about 1,000 km from Darwin, invalid and ordered the Pastoral Land Board to reassess it. Justice Natalie Charlesworth found the board exceeded its jurisdiction by approving a permit covering roughly 60,000 hectares—far larger than applied for—and failed to conduct an environmental impact assessment or afford procedural fairness. She rejected native title holders' arguments that activities fell outside 'farm tourism,' permitted observation of Aboriginal cultural works, and caused distress over sacred sites under section 24GB of the Native Title Act, while upholding the water licence from Rosie Creek.
items.title: Federal Court rules Lorella Springs tourism permit invalid

items.summary: Investigative journalist Patrick Radden Keefe, who has spent 20 years at The New Yorker and authored Say Nothing (2019), discusses his new book London Falling about a young impostor ensnared by money amid London's corruption. He warns that "we live in very mercenary times," where wealth justifies wrongdoing. Keefe argues truth remains essential for democracy, noting social media has fractured the shared reality needed to recognize it. Blaming opportunistic politicians like Donald Trump rather than legacy media for eroded trust, he sees an opening as audiences distrust screens. On AI, he refuses to let it touch his writing, telling young journalists that if their work is replaceable by machines, they are doing it badly.
items.title: Patrick Radden Keefe on the Decline of Truth and Trust in Journalism

items.summary: In May 2025, Finearom researchers analyzed 20 Colombian fruits to develop synthetic fragrances from over 2,000 raw materials. Sales director Mónica Castaño explained their olfactory-pyramid methodology. The company's flavors will soon reach a supermarket chain, symbolizing Colombia's roughly 2,500 fruit species—only about 5% commercially available. Environmental engineer and 'fruit guru' Gian Paolo Daguer has tasted over 400 varieties and urges government promotion of this bioeconomy through schools. Laboratory Phitother extracts chontaduro for sun protection containing omega-3, omega-6, vitamin E and polyphenols; technical director Luz Helena Núñez confirmed these properties. Chef Jefferson García created duck with papaya at Bogotá's Afluente restaurant.
items.title: Colombia's Untapped Fruit Biodiversity Drives Emerging Fragrance and Culinary Industry

items.summary: The Union government ordered sealing of 191 industrial units across Delhi and the National Capital Region for lacking air-pollution control equipment, directing secretary-level officers to inspect pollution measures in 15 cities. A particulate matter limit of 50 mg/Nm³ replaces March 2022 standards set at 80 mg/Nm³. At 8:05 am the average AQI was 351 (very poor), with eight of 58 stations above 400 and IIT Delhi worst at 426.
items.title: Delhi pollution: Centre orders closure of 191 industries for lack of emission control equipment

items.summary: A woman was seriously injured in Dattowal, Nalagarh area of Solan district, Himachal Pradesh. A car reportedly lost control at high speed and crashed into a parked vehicle along the roadside, sending it flying several metres directly into her as she walked past. The impact also overturned the speeding car. CCTV footage captured the collision, prompting panic among local residents who rushed to help and took her to hospital; her condition was not immediately known. Police have begun an investigation into how the driver lost control, with details of the cause still awaited.
items.title: Himachal Woman Injured as Speeding Car Sends Parked Vehicle into Her

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar recalled telling Prime Minister Narendra Modi he had no money to buy a ticket during a ride on Bengaluru's new Pink Line, prompting Modi to pay the fare. The incident followed Modi's November 13 inauguration of the line. Shivakumar described their relationship as one of personal regard and mutual respect, urging leaders to keep politics separate from development amid Karnataka-Centre funding disagreements.
items.title: 'I did not have money': Shivakumar recalls PM Modi paying his metro fare

items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed Sunday it targeted a US radar site at al-Riffa Air Base in Bahrain with six drones, per state media. No damage was reported. The statement came after Bahrain warned of an unspecified threat and urged residents to shelter. Iran also asserted the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and threatened harsher responses to any US aggression, amid ongoing tensions over navigation through the waterway.
items.title: Iran says it targeted US radar site in Bahrain with 6 drones

items.summary: A fire gutted around 25 shops in the woollens market at Ramlila Ground, Pataudi town, Gurugram on Sunday morning. Firefighters from Pataudi and Manesar brought the blaze under control after a woman heard noise around 4 am; no injuries were reported. The cause and full damage extent remain unknown. The annual market ran November to February, opened Nov 4 by the Himalayan Tribal Trade Association with vendors from Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.
items.title: Fire Gutted ~25 Shops at Gurugram's Pataudi Woollens Market

items.summary: A Sunday news roundup covers a stable US air traffic control system after a nationwide outage; the FAA reported airlines expected to cancel between 4,000 and 5,000 of roughly 41,000 scheduled flights as they repositioned aircraft and crews. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz while attempting an undetected passage. A trilateral meeting between Putin, Xi Jinping and Trump is set for Nov. 19 in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Elsewhere: Türkiye and allies condemned an Israeli strike on a Gaza medical complex; thousands protested Portugal's housing crisis across 32 cities; Italy fined Meta €805 million ($900 million) over Android data access; Pakistan reported killing 24 militants while RSF forces killed 10 civilians in Sudan. In sports, Denmark beat Portugal 4-1 to end their winning streak, and the Philippines won Eurovision Asia with 211 points.
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 15, 2026

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Congress president Manickam Tagore condemned Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar's speech at a Mysuru function asserting that a dam would be built across the Cauvery at Mekedatu. Tagore urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to object immediately, warning silence would betray Tamil Nadu and strain state relations. He alleged united opposition from Karnataka leaders but called for similar unity in Tamil Nadu against the Mekedatu project.
items.title: Tagore Condemns Karnataka CM's Speech on Mekedatu Dam

items.summary: The author reflects on childhood as a curated wonder-chamber of tactile, imaginative play and design. Early memories surface objects like engraved silver rattles, Channapatna lacquer toys, kaleidoscopes, brass buckets and matchbox ladybirds, set against an atelier-like home in Chennai where the mother archived presentations on floppy disks and demonstrated for civil liberties causes. Play ranged from Enid Blytonian bonfire cookouts to board games of deduction—Guess Who?, Mastermind, Operation—and drawing tools like Etch A Sketch and Spirograph. Television populated a pantheon: detectives such as Poirot and Byomkesh Bakshi; comedies including Fawlty Towers and The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air; and animation from Walt Disney to Jan Švankmajer and Hayao Miyazaki. Adolescence brought circuitry—Game Boy, Casio watches, iPods—and a design vocabulary spanning Charles and Ray Eames to Juicy Couture's gumball machines. Ultimately the author argues adults who dismiss play as puerile rely on its designers' ingenuity; like nested Matryoshka dolls, we accumulate rather than replace our former selves.
items.title: Winding the Wunderkammer: Springing Reveries

items.summary: On Sunday, the Central Railway's Mumbai division will run a megablock for essential engineering and maintenance work. Suburban services on the Main, Harbor and Trans-Harbor lines are affected; no block occurs on Western Railway suburban sections. The Main Line is disrupted from 11 am to 4 pm between Thane and Kalyan, with slow trains diverted to the fast line.
items.title: Mumbai Local Train Megablock Today: Services On Main, Harbour Line To Be Affected

items.summary: Rising Delhi-NCR pollution has driven air purifier demand up nearly fivefold, from four to about 20 units daily per shop. The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI), led by Chairman Brijesh Goyal and General Secretary Gurmeet Arora, says the current 18% GST on purifiers and HEPA filters is excessive and urged Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to cut it to 5%, classifying them as medical devices. With Delhi's AQI crossing 400—equated by doctors to smoking 20-25 cigarettes daily—the CTI also sought a Rs 5,000 crore pollution relief package and Rs 500 crore for installing purifiers in government institutions across 100 major markets.
items.title: Delhi Air Purifier Demand Surges as Traders Urge GST Cut Amid AQI Over 400

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a fresh warning as Cyclone Akvan—a low-pressure area named by Iran—develops over the southeast Bay of Bengal. Expected to strengthen into a cyclonic storm around November 16, it could bring winds reaching 50-70 kmph with gusts up to 85 kmph from November 17 onward. The system threatens weather conditions across the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Odisha, and parts of West Bengal.
items.title: Third Cyclone Threat Emerges Over Bay of Bengal After Arnab and Murasu

items.summary: The arrest of Yonca Verdioglu Sik, a German-born coordinator at the Heinrich Böll Foundation in Istanbul, illustrates how Turkey weaponizes espionage charges against critics. Although she was never questioned about spying, prosecutors scrutinized her foundation's finances and imposed a travel ban on her husband, Ahmet Sik—a member of parliament with immunity from TIP—suggesting pressure on him through his wife. This reflects a broader pattern since the 2016 coup attempt: journalists, opposition figures, activists, and foreign NGO staff face security charges that produce a chilling effect. Experts like Hakki Tas note these cases serve both domestic repression and hostage diplomacy against critics abroad.
items.title: Turkey Uses Espionage Accusations to Pressure Government Critics

items.summary: SOLRITE, a developer of virtual power plant (VPA) projects, together with Sonnen, announced the digital integration of VPP smart breakers managed by ADAPT Energy into the SOLRITE sonnen VPP. The expansion moves beyond battery storage to transform residential electrical loads into flexible, dispatchable grid assets and enables whole-home backup without hard-wired circuit relocation or exclusive load panels. With homeowner permission, the system can shed pre-approved household loads during both off-grid outages and on-grid VPP events using Eaton AbleEdge breakers, increasing dispatched injection into the grid by combining battery discharge with energy that would otherwise be consumed at home. The integration reduces installation complexity for crews while giving homeowners automatic load management without manual circuit resets.
items.title: Sonnen, SOLRITE, & ADAPT Energy, Integrating VPP Breakers to Turn Home Loads into Flexible Grid Assets

items.summary: The article examines how SpaceX, Elon Musk's ventures, is increasingly reliant on natural gas for rocket fuel production. The company is investing in pipelines like the 32.4-mile Coastal Connect Services project to Cape Canaveral and an 8-mile Starpipe pipeline in Texas, while also expanding into a new $100 billion city-and-launch-site called Starbase, Louisiana. Meanwhile, Tesla's Colossus data center in Memphis has spurred demand for gas generators, prompting environmental concerns over emissions. The piece highlights the tension between SpaceX's sustainability goals and its reliance on fossil fuels, as well as local opposition to projects like Starbase.
items.title: SpaceX and Tesla's Growing Dependence on Natural Gas Amid Environmental Concerns

items.summary: This workshop episode covers Kubernetes orchestration, where engineers describe desired state in deployment.yaml; the API server stores it in etcd; controllers reconcile desired versus actual state (e.g., four requested replicas become four pods); the scheduler assigns pods to worker nodes by CPU and memory availability; container runtimes download images while kubelet tracks node-to-pod assignments; Services provide stable endpoints exposed via Ingress or Gateway. The episode then contrasts single-agent systems—one reasoning LLM that plans, selects tools, and loops—with multi-agent orchestrators that split tasks across specialized agents for parallelism and verification. It also reviews the Testing Pyramid's three layers (unit, integration, E2E), explains how deep research coordinates sub-agents with synthesizer and citation roles, and outlines production guardrails: input screening, context verification, response generation, output validation (with up to two retries), and operational controls.
items.title: Kubernetes Explained for Busy Engineers and AI Agent Architectures

items.summary: Mozambique faces a structural education crisis, with classes held under trees or fragile structures amid an estimated 12,000 teacher deficit by 2025. Rainy-season disruptions (November to March) force calendar adjustments, while heat concentrates students during breaks. Only about 73 percent of the population has internet access as of 2024 data, and roughly one million students learn on the ground—constraints that limit AI adoption. Linguistic barriers compound this: only around 49 of Africa's 2,0,000 languages appear on platforms like Google Translate, though 81.7 percent speak a Bantu language at home versus Portuguese as sole official tongue. Advocates propose offline tools and digital assistants but stress that building schools, training teachers, and ensuring material access remain priorities over technology substitution.
items.title: AI in Mozambique's Tree-Top Classrooms: Infrastructure Gaps and Digital Promise

items.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye on November 13, 2026, IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol praised China as a clean-energy superpower. In an interview with China Media Group, he noted that geopolitical conflicts are accelerating energy transitions worldwide and highlighted Asia's focus on energy security amid the US-Iran conflict. He commended China's solar, wind, battery storage and EV advances for enabling affordable technology globally.
items.title: IEA Chief Hails China's Role in Global Energy Transition

items.summary: Tech giant Microsoft announced on Saturday that it had restored service following a massive global outage, attributing the disruption to elevated load rather than cyber or AI causes. The incident affected Outlook email, Teams and Copilot across at least 74 countries in the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, per monitoring site Downdetector. Microsoft also warned of an active phishing campaign exploiting fake service-notification emails.
items.title: Microsoft Restores Service After Global Outage

items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to propose creating an Asian version of the International Energy Agency (IEA) at Tuesday's 11-member Asia Zero Emission Community summit in Manila. The framework would coordinate oil stockpiling for energy crises, strengthening Asia's supply chains amid Middle East turmoil. Jakarta-based ERIA would serve as secretariat while Japan works with a new Tokyo IEA base to share expertise and set release rules.
items.title: Japan Proposes Asian Version of IEA at AZEC Summit

items.summary: Einar Tangen of CIGI examines allegations that Chinese intelligence recruited former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to gather information on Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang. Beijing has rejected the claims, which reportedly date to 2024 but gained attention after being briefed to President Trump in 2025. Tangen questions the absence of publicly available evidence and argues no facts have been established. He suggests three interests benefit: Trump seeking distraction from other issues; AI companies facing a potential write-down amid an inflated bubble, undermined by China's open-AI approach; and Congress pursuing restrictions after losing its pro-innovation stance in the election. Tangen finds it improbable that China is deliberately using this as cover.
items.title: Jensen Huang, Alice Huang and China spy allegation: Who benefits from the controversy?

items.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly built his tenure on intense pressure and autocratic rule, marked by abrasive office blowups and public dress-downs of senior leaders. His 33-year reign ended amid board scrutiny over personal conduct tied to a suspected Chinese intelligence link through Alice Huang. Colette Kress was named interim CEO while Harvey C. Jones became the first-ever board chair.
items.title: How Jensen Huang Dressed Down Executives Amid Nvidia's Leadership Collapse

items.summary: SpaceX's Starship completed its first-ever midair catch during the 15th test flight, returning to Texas on November 14 after completing 14 laps and deploying 26 Starlink satellites. Google CEO Sundar Pichai congratulated Elon Musk, calling it 'still feels like science fiction,' while NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman praised the achievement as 'almost magic.' The planned double catch fell short when a booster exploded shortly after liftoff on November 13.
items.title: Google CEO Congratulates SpaceX on First Starship Midair Catch

items.summary: Noel Tata, chairman of the trusts controlling Tata Group, questioned whether the conglomerate's major investments in semiconductors, aviation, electronics and EV batteries are being executed with sufficient discipline. The dispute over capital allocation, control and a possible listing has widened after the board backed Natarajan Chandrasekaran for another five-year term despite Noel Tata's opposition.
items.title: Tata Heir Questions Big Bets as US$185 Billion Group Feud Deepens

items.summary: Debt recovery agencies are pursuing unpaid invoices tied to Thomas Hong, founder and CEO of the Lao Huo Tang restaurant group. FDR Services is chasing about $550,795.58 from three suppliers across several outlets; its reported total rose from an initial $539,810.91 after adding a meat supplier's claims. Separately, A.S.K Debt Recovery handles claims approaching $2 million involving multiple clients and creditors of the group's businesses. Collections have been difficult: collectors faced empty premises, disputes over Hong's directorship, and legal correspondence disputing his involvement. The commercial debts are distinct from separate CPF arrears cases and a High Court winding-up order against Singapura Heritage Food Hall.
items.title: Debt collectors pursue claims exceeding $2m linked to Lao Huo Tang

items.summary: On Saturday, SpaceX made history by catching its Starship spacecraft upright in the mechanical arms of its launch tower's 'Mechazilla' after a successful 15th flight from Starbase in Texas. The Super Heavy booster ascended under 33 Raptor engines before diverting offshore following an automated abort; it reignited 32 of its planned 33 engines for boostback but ended the burn early due to low fuel mass, with the cause under investigation. In orbit, Starship deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and remained aloft over 20 hours before returning approximately 22.5 hours after launch. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and NASA administrator Jared Isaacman praised the milestone as an almost magical step toward fully reusable rockets.
items.title: SpaceX Starship Achieves Historic Tower Catch on Its 15th Flight

items.summary: Jensen Huang's abrasive leadership drew mixed reactions after his resignation, which followed an affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. Reports from the New York Post describe verbal abuse and outbursts at meetings, including telling executive Jay Puri he hoped to die. Biographer Stephen Witt said Huang cloaked arrogance behind a humble persona. Colette Kress now serves as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
items.title: 'I hope you die': Jensen Huang told Indian-origin Nvidia VP during a meeting

items.summary: Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan warns that India should not expect a major rollback of US tariffs, even after President Donald Trump's party suffered a sweeping defeat in the November 3 midterms.
