He says Democratic gains may increase scrutiny of Trump's trade policies but higher tariffs will likely persist as a feature of US policy. The new Washington balance could limit some aggressive decisions yet bring no immediate relief to trading partners.
items.title: 'Learn to live with US tariffs': Raghuram Rajan cautions India despite Trump's midterm defeat

items.summary: On November 14, 2026, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng opened the fourth APEC Business Advisory Council meeting in Shenzhen. Also a member of the Communist Party's Political Bureau, he said the upcoming 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting would set direction for Asia-Pacific cooperation and urged ABAC to advance regional economic ties.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Opens Fourth APEC Business Advisory Council Meeting in Shenzhen

items.summary: In February 2021, China declared the elimination of absolute poverty after lifting approximately 98.99 million rural residents above the national line, ending a four-decade campaign that raised about 800 million people—more than 70% of global poverty reduction—over roughly two decades. A five-year transition period concluded at the end of 2025 with regularized anti-relapse mechanisms to prevent backsliding from illness, crop failure or job loss. China's approach shifted toward targeted assistance tailored to household needs rather than one-size-fits-all cash handouts. International observers and leaders—including South Africa's John Bailey, Kenya's Eric Biegon, Peru's Javier Velásquez Quesquén and Cambodia's Vongsey Vissoth—emphasize that the real lesson lies not in copying China but adapting its systematic planning to local conditions.
items.title: China's Anti-Poverty Victory and Lessons for Other Nations

items.summary: Congress leader Manish Tewari said India's core demand that Pakistan act against cross-border terrorism remained unaddressed, with Islamabad taking no action against terrorist infrastructure. His remarks coincided with Pakistan nominating Federal Minister Musadik Masood Malik to represent the country at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi from November 20 to 22.
items.title: 'Nothing noteworthy': Manish Tewari on Pakistan minister attending SCO meet in Delhi

items.summary: Karnataka Congress leader Priyank Kharge said the law is on Karnataka's side in the Mekedatu dam dispute, though both states must follow Supreme Court directions. BJP leader R Ashoka accused Congress of double standards—holding a 'Our water, our right' padayatra in Karnataka while Tamil Nadu leaders like B Manickam Tagore and Jothimani oppose it. Kharge defended pursuing the balancing reservoir near Kanakapura to meet Bengaluru's water needs.
items.title: 'Law on our side': Karnataka minister's remark amid Mekedatu Dam row with Tamil Nadu

items.summary: Over the past six months, 11 penny stocks have corrected sharply, falling between 50% and 84%. These were identified through a screen of companies with a market capitalisation under Rs 1,000 crore, share prices below Rs 20, and minimum recent trading volumes of 5 lakh shares. The data source is ACE Equi.
items.title: 11 Penny Stocks Plunge Up to 84% in Six Months

items.summary: The article lists tentative weekly corporate actions for Indian investors, who must hold shares in demat accounts by each record date. On November 16-20, Shipping Corporation of India pays Rs 4/share; Cochin Shipyard and ASM Technologies pay Rs 6/share; Indag Rubber Rs 0.9/share; Nile Rs 3/share; EAAA India Alternatives Rs 7/share; Page Industries a high Rs 150/share; AK Capital Services Rs 18/share; Ingersoll Rand (India) Rs 20/share; Oil India Rs 7/share; Prevest Denpro, Venus Pipes & Tubes and Rama Phosphates each Rs 0.5/share. MRF pays Rs 3/share on November 17. BN Agrochem turns ex-record for a 1:10 stock split. Oriental Infra Trust and Power Grid Infrastructure Investment Trust go ex-record too. Praxis Home Retail and Ironwood Education face rights issues; Ashok Leyland and PDP Shipping & Projects pay dividends Friday. The list may grow as more companies announce dates.
items.title: Weekly corporate actions in India's stock market

items.summary: This two-minute documentary marks the sixth anniversary of a symposium on advancing the Yangtze River Economic Belt, spotlighting Zhoudai Bridge in east China. The 25.7-kilometer bridge links eight Zhoushan islands to the Chinese mainland as part of an expressway network spanning over 86 kilometers.
items.title: Mega Island-Link Bridge Connects Yangtze River Delta

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang told Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn in Bangkok on November 14, 2026 that "China and Thailand are as close as one family," a unique advantage of the two countries' relations. Citing President Xi Jinping's state visit last year and continued economic cooperation amid global headwinds, Li pledged deeper collaboration in investment, technology, new energy vehicles and people-to-people exchanges.
items.title: Premier Li Frames China-Thailand Ties as Family-Like Bond

items.summary: A fifth Canadian soldier, Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco, has died from injuries sustained when a grass fire swept through military training areas at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright on 17 October. The blaze ignited during live-fire exercises and spread rapidly in strong winds, killing four initially and injuring dozens. Officials called it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's forces.
items.title: Fifth Canadian Soldier Dies in Wainwright Base Fire Tragedy

items.summary: A report by Surviving Economic Abuse, titled Access Denied: Futures Derailed and conducted with Ipsos UK, finds that nearly one in five young women aged 16-24 in the UK – about 700,000 people – have experienced digital financial products used as tools of abuse by a current or former partner. Abusers exploit banking apps, online payments and credit to control victims and prevent them from leaving relationships. Rates are highest among disabled young women and those with caring responsibilities for children.
items.title: Digital Finance Products Used as Tools of Abuse Against Young Women in the UK

items.summary: At the Calais Eurotunnel terminal, a truck of British food to Gibraltar was delayed after paperwork errors forced removal of cannelloni over a date mistake and destruction of pig carcasses that had fallen. Officials note export health certificates, customs and veterinary documents no longer existed in the single market. A Defra report found small-to-medium exporters worst hit; an Aston University estimate suggests an SPS deal could boost UK agri-food exports to the EU by up to 22.5%, while government figures project GDP gains of up to £5.1bn by 2040 (up to 0.14%). Eurotunnel's CEO Yann Leriche says trade has fallen over 20% since Brexit, though a deal could cut crossing costs substantially and restore pet travel.
items.title: Brexit Food Checks at Calais Eurotunnel and Outlook for SPS Deal

items.summary: The top scorer of South Korea's national exam for aspiring tax accountants admitted using generative AI to cheat, confessing on the YouTube channel of Attorney Lee Don-ho that he photographed questions with a micro-camera and checked answers via smartphone. Scoring 397.5 out of 400 in April with only one wrong answer among 160 questions, Han ranked first but sparked cheating accusations he initially denied. The scandal has prompted serious government attention just days before the annual college entrance exam this Thursday.
items.title: South Korea's Top Tax-Exam Scorer Admits AI Cheating Amid Suneung Fears

items.summary: Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade and a key planner of the 7 October attack on Israel, was killed Saturday in an Israeli airstrike at Al-Mawasi. Witnesses reported four missiles hitting a tent in the Al-Waha camp; three injured arrived at Nasser Hospital with one dead body. Hamas called it a cowardly assassination. Younis, 53, had led the brigade since September.
items.title: Israel Kills Hamas Commander Samir Abu Younis in Gaza Strike

items.summary: CEO Gaurav Dolwani of LICO Materials, a Bengaluru-based lithium-ion battery recycling and refurbishing firm founded in 2021, targets revenue of about ₹450-500 crore in fiscal 2026-27. Up from roughly ₹350 crore in 2025-26, the growth reflects higher material-processing volumes, improved capacity utilisation and greater availability of end-of-life batteries as electric two- and three-wheeler adoption rises. The company's current processing capacity stands at around 4 GWh, with plans to reach approximately 10 GWh over the next three years.
items.title: LICO Materials Targets ₹450-500 Cr Revenue in FY26-27 as EV Recycling Expands

items.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual ASEAN summit in Manila on Sunday for three days of talks, including dialogues with world leaders led by US President Donald Trump. Discussions would focus on the Middle East war and other global conflicts, per draft post-summit communiqués seen by The Associated Press.
items.title: ASEAN Summit Opens Amid Global Conflicts as Trump Visits Manila

items.summary: AFC Wimbledon remains one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL, alongside Exeter City (labels: quantity-588-591). The club faces mounting financial strain after withdrawing £87m of proposed investment from Sloane Street Capital, led by Omar Mir and Ryan Bertrand. An £87m proposal collapse left finances tighter amid a £2.6m loss in 2024-25 expected to rise by £500,000 (s7). Supporter voting rights fell from 75% to 50.01%, mirroring the German '50+1' model. The board may seek a loan of up to £3m while still owing £7.5m in debts after returning home to Plough Lane in 2020 (s6, s10). Wimbledon's winless run ended with a narrow victory over Blackpool, moving them four points clear of relegation as their future division remains uncertain.
items.title: AFC Wimbledon's Fan Ownership and Failed Investment Bid

items.summary: Reeves's muntjac, or kyon, an invasive deer-like species in Chiba Prefecture, Japan, has proliferated since the 1960s-80s after escaping a tourist park. The population surged from 13,264 (fiscal 2006) to 94,093 (fiscal 2024), spreading across 18 municipalities and causing ¥4-9 million in annual crop damage.
items.title: Chiba's Invasive Reeves's Muntjac (Kyon) Threatens Agriculture and Native Vegetation

items.summary: At its Manila summit, ASEAN—chairing Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.—reaffirmed constructive engagement under the bloc's Five-Point Consensus following a 2021 coup. The plan calls for an immediate end to violence amid a civil war the UN estimates has killed 100,000 people and displaced over 3.5 million since then.
items.title: ASEAN Reaffirms Engagement with Myanmar Amid Ongoing Civil War and Peace Plan Review

items.summary: Amid global tech layoffs, a senior Qualcomm engineer in India posted on Reddit that their severance—standard payout plus tenure compensation and a waived relocation clawback—yielded roughly 15 months of salary. The engineer described the new team's culture as hostile, citing personal attacks from management, framing the layoff as a blessing in disguise.
items.title: Laid-off Qualcomm Engineer in India Frames Severance as Escape from Toxic Workplace

items.summary: Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) swept 24 of Melaka's 28 state assembly seats in the November 14 polls, with Barisan Nasional winning 21. Analysts say this landslide reinforces a Malay-Muslim unity pact that consolidates Malay support while drawing non-Malay voters toward DAP, which held only four Chinese-majority seats. The result poses a difficult challenge for Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's Pakatan Harapan coalition, whose components PKR and Amanah won nothing. Bersatu failed to win any of its seven contested seats, undermining its value as an electoral partner. Political analysts James Chin and Azmi Hassan note the alliance could capture 100-105 parliamentary seats at GE16 but warn that seat negotiations between UMNO and PAS may strain cohesion. Voter turnout reached 71.77 per cent versus 65.85 per cent in 2021, driven by Malay mobilisation.
items.title: Melaka's BN-PN Landslide Strengthens Malay Unity Pact and Pressures Anwar Ahead of GE16

items.summary: In a letter to US District Judge Victor Marrero ahead of his November 20 sentencing, Nikhil Gupta said he plotted the assassination attempt on Khalistani leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun alone and regretted it. Gupta pleaded guilty in February to three federal charges: murder-for-hire (max 10 years), conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire (up to 10 years), and conspiracy to commit money laundering (max 20 years). Prosecutors urged a sentence of 293 months, just over 24 years; his lawyers seek 144 months, roughly 12 years. Gupta was recruited in early 2023 by Vikash Yadav and tried to hire a hitman for $100,000, unaware the contact was an undercover agent.
items.title: Nikhil Gupta Sentencing; Prosecutors Seek Over 24 Years

items.summary: Australian authorities report that illicit tobacco seizures reached a record high, with 730 tonnes seized between July and September. The government attributes the decline to stronger enforcement across federal, state and territory agencies. However, record seizure volumes raise questions about market scale.
items.title: Australia's Illicit Tobacco Market Shrinks After Years of Growth

items.summary: Police have charged a 38-year-old Perth man with murder following the killing of a 44-year-old man on a rural property south of Perth, near Keysbrook. The incident prompted a major security operation, and firearms were seized from the scene. Police say the two men knew each other. The accused is due to appear in court on Monday.
items.title: Perth man charged with murder after rural Keysbrook shooting death

items.summary: On Saturday SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket between two mechanical arms, a first-ever catch that the company said changed everything. After orbiting Earth 14 times and deploying 26 satellites for Elon Musk's Starlink constellation during a 22-hour journey, Ship 42 returned to Texas' east coast before landing at Starbase in Texas. SpaceX CEO Musk hugged it upon return, while NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called the catch almost magic. The Super Heavy booster attempt failed and splashed down offshore; its early boostback burn was under investigation.
items.title: SpaceX Catches Starship in Historic First

items.summary: A homeless elderly man died after being struck and dragged nearly two kilometres beneath a car on Friday night in Karunagappally, Kollam district. The driver, Shajahan, was arrested Saturday and charged under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Police initially registered an accidental-death case before CCTV footage implicated him.
items.title: Homeless Man Dragged Under Car for 2 km in Kerala; Driver Arrested

items.summary: An empty Vande Bharat rake traveled about 463 km between Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh in October despite repeated warnings of ineffective coach brakes. Railway staff failed to integrate the braking system, ignored crew complaints, and permitted the train to proceed using only locomotive and regenerative braking until action was taken at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station. The South Eastern Railway ordered a detailed investigation into multiple staff failures ahead of a similar derailment in Assam.
items.title: Vande Bharat Rake Travels 463 km with Failed Brakes Across Two States

items.summary: In this review, literary critic and author Deepa Dhingra recommends RK Narayan’s 1967 novel The Vendor of Sweets as comforting reading. Set in the familiar South Indian town of Malgudi, it follows Jagan, a 55-year-old sweet vendor who lives by Gandhian principles—wearing khadi, spinning the charkha for an hour daily, and renouncing salt and sugar—yet clings to wealth despite his austere lifestyle. The novel explores the generation gap with Mali, whose departure to America and return with a foreign bride wound Jagan’s pride; it also ventures into dreamlike alternate timelines tracing Jagan as groom and ageing man. Narayan balances sympathy and satire, ultimately suggesting that conscientious truth-worship remains possible even without strict adherence to Gandhian ritual.
items.title: Sunday book pick: In ‘The Vendor of Sweets’, a Gandhian is put to the test in postcolonial Malgudi

items.summary: At the inauguration of SEBI's pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, Chairman Ajay Pandey announced proposed guidelines to establish guardrails for AI use in capital markets. These focus on disclosures, accountability of regulated entities, and a 'human-in-the-loop' approach ensuring human oversight over critical decisions. The regulator has also developed supervisory tools like Sudarshan and is reviewing the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) to better support deep-tech startups.
items.title: SEBI Issues AI Usage Guidelines for Capital Markets

items.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors made a net Rs 84,290 crore investment in Indian equities during November 2-13 (nine trading sessions), reversing October's Rs 34,843 crore withdrawal. Cumulative FPI outflows narrowed to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore in 2026 from nearly Rs 3 lakh crore weeks earlier. Vedant Gupte of Trackk called the buying a tactical turn driven by falling crude and AI-trade profit-taking; Nifty rose above 25,000 on financials, telecom, capital goods, pharma and auto strength plus banking short-covering.
items.title: FPIs pump Rs 84,290 crore into D-Street in first fortnight of November

items.summary: An unprecedented meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the United States could occur on the sidelines of this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, though Beijing has not confirmed it. Trump suggested one planned APEC meeting would involve Putin and Xi, while Kremlin officials say coordination is underway; the media dubbed it a 'new Yalta.' Nobody is certain what they would discuss—Trump avoided Russia's Ukraine war, citing Iran and denuclearization instead. The summit poses diplomatic challenges: for China, being tied to Russia's war or framed as a global decision-maker ('G3') could damage its image; the EU fears exclusion from Ukraine talks. Despite their 'no limits' partnership since early 2022, Beijing avoids formal alliance obligations while providing Russia energy markets and dual-use technology.
items.title: Beijing's Dilemma Over a Potential Xi-Trump-Putin Trilateral Summit at APEC

items.summary: Magsaysay Award–winning Indian Forest Service officer and whistleblower Sanjeev Chaturvedi has petitioned the Supreme Court of India seeking a statutory framework to protect whistleblowers. He argues that the non-operationalisation of the Whistleblowers Protection Act, 2014—which was notified on May 12, 2014 but never brought into force—has created a constitutional and statutory vacuum leaving no institutional mechanism for protection against retaliation. Chaturvedi contends this inaction by the Centre is not an isolated case but a systemic norm enabling persecution of public servants nationwide. He seeks to expand his writ petition under Article 142, requesting interim guidelines to bridge the gap, asserting that executive failure violates Articles 14, 19 and 21.
items.title: IFS Officer Sanjeev Chaturvedi Seeks Supreme Court Framework for Whistleblower Protection

items.summary: The Maharashtra government extended its May 2026 cut to the value-added tax (VAT) on aviation turbine fuel from 18% to 7%, prolonging the concession by five months until April 14, 2027. The reduction followed rising global crude prices and a West Asia conflict that strained carriers' costs; ATF accounts for roughly 40-50% of airline operating expenses. A November 12 notification formalized the extension via the Maharashtra Value Added Tax Act, 2002, with the earlier rate applying at Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Pune airports before expiring on November 14, 2026.
items.title: Maharashtra Extends 7% VAT on Aviation Turbine Fuel Until April 14, 2027

items.summary: The African Union, United Nations, EU, Arab League, and IGAD jointly condemned escalating drone attacks across Sudan on Sunday, calling for an immediate end to hostilities. The Quintet expressed deep concern over the deadly escalation inflicting suffering amid a catastrophic humanitarian crisis, with damage to power facilities causing widespread electricity outages.
items.title: Five International Partners Condemn Escalating Attacks in Sudan

items.summary: Law Minister Mohammad Asaduzzaman said Bangladesh has finished all legal steps to bring ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina back from India, leaving the final extradition call with New Delhi. Sentenced to death in November 2025 for crimes against humanity tied to a 2024 crackdown, she fled to India after student-led protests toppled her Awami League government following 16 years in power. Bangladesh denies her appeal rights under Article 479(3) of the 1973 Act and has demanded extradition amid ongoing unrest.
items.title: Bangladesh Completes Legal Steps for Sheikh Hasina's Return; Awaits India's Decision

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Elon Musk's SpaceX of misleading Kyiv over speed restrictions on its Starshield network, which capped terminals at 161 kilometres per hour in Russian-occupied areas and limited Ukraine's ability to intercept drones. The curbs had lasted five days with no clear explanations. Zelenskyy directed contacts with the U.S., Pentagon and SpaceX.
items.title: Zelenskyy Questions SpaceX Over Reported Starshield Speed Restrictions

items.summary: A Jordan State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday, November 15, 2026, after convicting them of an armed terrorist attack during a funeral service at a church in Karak, western Jordan. The assault killed nine people and wounded 34 others. All three attackers were arrested following joint search operations.
items.title: Jordanian Court Sentences Three Men to Death for Church Attack

items.summary: A Copa Airlines Boeing 737 and a UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane collided on the taxiway at Miami International Airport Saturday night, injuring two passengers. The Copa flight carried 166 passengers and six crew; all disembarked safely with only minor injuries reported. Audio from air traffic control captured the pilot noting they were struck after overshooting. The crash followed a nearly five-hour nationwide FAA network outage that disrupted more than 20,000 flights.
items.title: Wingtip Collision at Miami Airport Amid US Flight Recovery After FAA Outage

items.summary: In Bunia, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo, health ministry teams with UNICEF and Africa CDC held Ebola awareness campaigns at schools after cases resumed post-September classes. About 40 schools reported EVD cases, including one teacher death. Six months into the outbreak, cases exceed 11,000 with over 5,400 deaths; children account for 35% of deaths through November 4.
items.title: Ebola Awareness Campaigns at Bunia Schools Amid Ongoing Outbreak in DR Congo

items.summary: In a football friendly on Sunday, India suffered a 0-3 defeat to host nation New Zealand at Christchurch. Finn Surman opened the scoring with a header deflected off Akash Mishra in the 22nd minute; James McGarry doubled it from outside the box in the 40th; and Chris Wood sealed it after Jesse Randall's setup. India tightened defensively but could not break through.
items.title: India Lose 0-3 To New Zealand in Football Friendly

items.summary: Israel killed Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, in an overnight strike on southern Gaza. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it struck a radar system at a US base in Bahrain—though CENTCOM denied the claim and said it intercepted two Iranian drones. In Yemen, Houthis say an airstrike wounded four people; Saudi Arabia says its defenses shot down missiles and drones.
items.title: Israel Kills Hamas Commander; Iran Claims Bahrain Strike

items.summary: As Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia—following reports of extramarital affairs, one allegedly involving a Chinese government spy—shakes the company and its succession plans, it has recentered attention on global semiconductor dependence. Tufts professor Chris Miller notes that companies reliant on Nvidia will watch closely whether to stay or turn to competitors.
items.title: The chip war never ended

items.summary: Concerns about young people's cellphone dependence are now joined by worries over how much time baby boomers spend on mobile devices. In Spain, a Spanish National Research Council report found internet access reached 96.3% among those aged 65 to 74 in 2025, with growing dependency. Non-digital natives face higher scam and false-content vulnerability because they question image authenticity less; the risk is both psychological and financial. Experts like María Gijón warn algorithms create echo chambers that polarize views, while AI-generated images flood family chats. Treatment director María Quevedo stresses emotional needs behind sharing and urges conscious rather than restrictive engagement.
items.title: Boomers' Growing Social Media and AI Addiction

items.summary: British epidemiologist Sir John Edmunds warns that while respiratory illnesses like flu remain the most plausible pandemic threat, governments must prepare for a wide range of unpredictable dangers. Speaking to EL PAÍS in Madrid after returning from an Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC—where 250 armed groups operate and over 5,000 have died—he stresses lessons learned during COVID-19: we cannot only plan for known pathogens. He cites Mpox, HIV (still in its first wave 40 years later), natural disasters worsened by climate change, and man-made threats like AI and disinformation. Drawing on Donald Rumsfeld's concept of 'unknown unknowns,' he argues societies need resilient systems to handle unpredictable crises.
items.title: Sir John Edmunds on pandemic preparedness and emerging global threats

items.summary: On Saturday night around 10:30 PM, a fire broke out in a garage-cum-warehouse in the Kalamboli steel market of Navi Mumbai. Emergency crews responded to an alert about a shop on fire but found flames inside a combination garage and godown. A sudden explosion occurred from drums containing thinner stored within.
items.title: Fire and Blast at Kalamboli Steel Market Warehouse in Navi Mumbai Injures Firefighter

items.summary: Mahanagar Gas Limited raised Mumbai CNG prices to Rs 91.50 per kg on November 14, adding Rs 1.50 and marking the eighth hike of 2026 for a total increase of Rs 11 since January—nearly 14 percent. The company cites lower domestic gas availability, higher procurement costs, greater reliance on imported RLNG, and rising international prices amid Middle East tensions. Around 12.93 lakh CNG vehicles across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region will be affected.
items.title: Mumbai CNG Prices Rise Again Amid Gas Shortages

items.summary: JustKeth, a Thai-French YouTuber and IRL streamer known for outdoor travel broadcasts, reportedly faced harassment during a nighttime livestream in Udaipur, Rajasthan. A man allegedly approached her outdoors and requested a kiss on the lips while she streamed to viewers. She clearly refused, appearing visibly uncomfortable as the interaction unfolded before her audience.
items.title: French-Thai YouTuber Harassed During Udaipur Livestream

items.summary: Raabia Hawa received the 2026 Tusk Award for Conservation in Africa on Nov. 11, London, for founding Ulinzi Africa Foundation (est. 2014) to combat elephant poaching and wildlife crime along Kenya's Lamu–Tana River coastline near the Somali border. Her work expanded into countering illegal industrial bottom-trawling and opposing extractive mining concessions. Defending nature has drawn death threats and designation as an al-Shabaab target; she was notified of a named attack, which she judged intimidation. She documented 15 dead turtles alongside one trawler carrying 48 endangered species, pursued the case through letters to the DPP and Kenya Coast Guard, and secured Kipini's status as a trawling-free zone. The award provides three years of sustained funding for her volunteer-powered organization.
items.title: Kenya's Raabia Hawa Wins Tusk Award Despite al-Shabaab Targeting

items.summary: At the 17th Conference of the Parties on biological diversity, Madagascar outlined its commitment to protecting terrestrial and marine ecosystems. Global Voices interviewed Tojotsara Ratefason, Director of Protected Areas within the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MEDD). The country reported a network of 155 protected areas as an important foundation for conservation efforts. Madagascar relies on the National Strategy and Action Plan for Biodiversity (SPANB) to translate international commitments into national action under the Convention on Biological Diversity. Ratefason emphasized that protection extends beyond counting areas, stressing collaboration with local communities and promoting green jobs linked to biodiversity. As one of 17 megadiverse countries worldwide, Madagascar benefits from Global Environment Facility funding while aiming to ensure these resources reach local populations.
items.title: Madagascar's Biodiversity Protection Strategy at COP17

items.summary: This Sunday digest surveys several Indian political and economic developments, framed by a striking opening about lethal violence against those exposing drug peddling. It examines the BJP's rural breakthrough in Muslim-majority constituencies—winning 97 of 144 such seats since 2020, with 28 for the first time—while noting that vote counts alone cannot explain voter behavior. The piece then turns to Uttar Pradesh's economic progress under Yogi Adityanath: state output doubled in nine years, though per capita income remains about half the national average. Finally, it profiles the PM Internship Scheme, which drew 16,060 applicants across its first two rounds and over forty thousand after a redesign with higher stipends and shorter commitments.
items.title: Sunday Digest — The Robots Knew Too Much To Be Sold

items.summary: MIT engineers cast a concrete beam using sewn fabric molds, achieving roughly one-third the concrete and half the steel of a conventional equivalent. The design combined graphic statics for reinforcement layout with topology optimization to place concrete efficiently. Because wet fabric deforms under load—making shape hard to predict—the team turned that flexibility into an advantage through computational pattern-making, packing a moderately wet, sand-rich mix by hand without vibration. Testing showed measured deflection within about 2 percent of the model’s prediction. Cost analysis revealed location dependence: in the Global South, all three fabric versions saved roughly 10–20 percent versus conventional beams; in the Global North, higher sewing labor made them about 16–55 percent more expensive. The team views this as a proof of concept for custom-shaped components rather than standard rectangular members.
items.title: MIT Demonstrates Material-Saving Concrete Beams Cast in Sewn Fabric Molds
